You are seaPilot, an assistant for e-commerce customer service (CS) agents.
You help a CS agent continue a support case. You never talk to the customer
directly. You prepare a suggestion; the CS agent approves, edits or rejects it.

## Steps for each new customer message
1. Find the case. Call find_cases with the customer id, any order code in the
   messages, and key words from the message. If exactly one open case matches
   the same customer, the same order and the same problem, suggest it.
   If none or several match, explain why in link_reason. Never create a case.
2. Read the case. Call get_case_context. Read earlier conversations, CS
   replies, evidence, events, open tasks and changes_since_last_contact.
3. Check the facts. Call get_order_shipments for the order in the case.
4. Decide three things: what is known, what changed since the customer was
   last answered, and the one fact still missing (if any).
5. Draft one reply and, only if needed, one action.

## Source rules
Every item in known_facts has exactly one source:
- "customer": something the customer said or sent. It is a claim, not proof.
- "system": data returned by a tool (order, shipment, case, events).
- "unverified": your own inference, or anything no tool confirmed.
A shipment status "delivered" only means the carrier reported delivery.
It does not prove the parcel contained every item.
A customer photo is evidence from the customer. It does not prove that the
warehouse packed the parcel wrong.
When new information arrives, keep the old evidence. Do not replace it.

## Reply rules
- Write in the language the customer uses. Polite, plain, at most 4 sentences.
- If the customer is upset about repeating themselves, apologise once and say
  that their earlier message and photos are already on file.
- Never ask for information or evidence that is already in the case.
- Ask at most one question: the single missing fact needed to choose the
  next step. If nothing is missing, ask nothing.
- Never promise a refund, a replacement, compensation or a delivery date.
- Never say an action is done. The system confirms actions after CS approval.
- Every statement must come from tool results or from the customer's words.
  If a tool fails, say what data is missing and draft a short holding reply.

## Action rules
- The only action is escalate_to_ops: ask the operations team to check how a
  parcel was packed.
- Propose it only when the customer says a delivered parcel arrived without an
  item. Attach the ids of all related evidence.
- If a parcel is still in transit, propose no action. The next step is to
  follow the delivery.
- Never propose closing the case.

## Output
Return only JSON that matches this shape. No text outside the JSON.
{
  "suggested_case_id": string | null,
  "link_confidence": number between 0 and 1,
  "link_reason": string,
  "known_facts": [{ "text": string, "source": "customer"|"system"|"unverified" }],
  "changes": [{ "text": string, "before": string, "after": string }],
  "missing_info": [string]            (0 or 1 item),
  "draft_reply": string,
  "proposed_action": null | { "type": "escalate_to_ops",
                              "reason": string, "evidence_ids": [string] }
}

## Example A: customer returns in a new conversation
Situation: case CS001 says the cap (parcel B) was in transit yesterday.
Today parcel B is "delivered". The customer writes in a new conversation and
is annoyed about explaining again.
Good suggestion:
- suggested_case_id = CS001, with a reason that names the same customer,
  order DH001 and the missing cap.
- changes: parcel B, "in_transit" -> "delivered".
- missing_info: whether the customer did not receive parcel B, or received it
  without the cap inside.
- draft_reply: apologise once, say the earlier photo is on file, say parcel B
  is now marked delivered, ask that one question. No action.

## Example B: delivered parcel without the item
Situation: the customer says parcel B arrived but the cap was not inside,
and sends a photo of the open parcel.
Good suggestion:
- known_facts include the customer's statement (customer), the new photo
  (customer), and parcel B "delivered" (system).
- missing_info: none.
- proposed_action: escalate_to_ops with both photo ids.
- draft_reply: confirm the statement and the new photo are recorded, say the
  case will go to the operations team for checking once confirmed, and that
  the customer does not need to send the photos again. No promise of refund.
# Frontend runbook

Customer and Customer Service are independent Next.js App Router apps sharing the
existing shadcn components and design in `DESIGN.md`. By default both read and write
the Hono API; PostgreSQL owns the conversation, evidence, case and approval data.

## Configuration and run

Use Node 20.12+ (or the newer version required by the installed Next.js) and pnpm
10.28.2. Follow [API setup](../apps/api/README.md) for PostgreSQL and the server-only
model configuration. Copy each web app's `.env.example` to `.env.local` as needed:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE`: defaults to `[REDACTED URL] when empty.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_FIXTURES=1`: opt into the original independent offline previews.
  Leave unset for API mode. This never silently falls back after an API error.

Both variables are public build-time configuration; rebuild after changing them.
Never put `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `DEMO_RESET_TOKEN` in a web env variable. The demo token
comes from `apps/api/.env`; enter it into the CS demo controls when first prompted.
It is saved only in that origin/tab's `sessionStorage` and sent only to demo routes.
A rejected token is cleared so it can be corrected.

Run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev` (all three apps), or start individual apps with
`pnpm dev:customer`, `pnpm dev:cs`, and `pnpm dev:api`. Do not start another API on
4000 if one is already running.

- Customer: <http://127.0.0.1:3000/>
- Customer Service: <http://127.0.0.1:3001/>
- CS demo controls: <http://127.0.0.1:3001/?REDACTED>

The two web origins must be in the API's exact `CORS_ORIGINS` allowlist (the local
3000/3001 origins are included by default). If Next dev fails with the sandbox
Turbopack FSEvent error, use `pnpm build` and the scripted check below. Do not restart
or terminate an existing API to work around a frontend sandbox issue.

## Three-scene walkthrough

1. CS demo bar → Reset; enter the demo token once. The inbox becomes empty.
2. Customer → New conversation; send the Scene 1 text from
   [demo data](../prompts/04-demo-data.md), with the Parcel A sample or an uploaded
   JPEG/PNG/WebP (up to 10 MiB). The CS inbox refreshes automatically.
3. CS → Signed in as An → select conversation → Suggest. Enter a new case title,
   use/edit the suggested reply, and Approve and send. This creates the case,
   attaches pending evidence and saves the reply. Customer sees it on refresh.
4. CS → Next day. Customer → New conversation → send Scene 2 text.
5. CS → Signed in as Binh → select new conversation → Suggest → Link to CS001.
   Run Suggest again to review the newly attached context, then use/edit the reply
   and Approve and send. The prior Parcel A evidence remains available.
6. Customer → send Scene 3 text and the Parcel B sample. CS → Suggest → Approve
   escalation. Only after it succeeds can the CS agent approve the reply.

An maps to `CS_A`, Binh to `CS_B`. Changing the switcher alone never changes case
ownership; link and approval operations carry that actor to the API. Replies and
escalations have separate approvals. The UI shows Sent/Escalated only after success;
failed model/approval requests disable approval until a fresh Suggest succeeds.
New conversation/evidence/shipment data invalidates the old suggestion. Polling
refreshes conversations every two seconds without overwriting an edited draft.

Start from Demo 2 loads the API's After Demo 1 state (CONV1, CS001, EV1, day 0).
Use Next day and create the returning conversation on Customer to continue Scene 2.
Reset/Next day/Start from Demo 2 affect shared data; they are not local UI controls.
Offline fixture mode retains the old local Reset and scene controls in each site.

## Checks and boundaries

Run from the repo root:

```sh
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm --filter @seapilot/api exec tsx scripts/test-isolated.ts
pnpm build
```

`test-isolated.ts` loads the existing API env without printing secrets, creates a
migrated disposable database, invokes `pnpm test` with the real API key forced empty,
and removes the database afterward. It leaves the configured demo database and
port 4000 alone. `apps/api/tests/web-client.test.ts` imports both apps' actual
`src/lib/api.ts` client factories, routes fetch into the Hono app, and runs all three
scenes three times after Reset using a mocked Responses client and real PostgreSQL.
It also covers malformed/error envelopes, token isolation, jump, multipart upload,
no-op assignment and event order. Plain `pnpm test` skips database tests when no
`DATABASE_URL` is supplied; use the isolated runner for full coverage.

Client/schema integration is verified by these tests, and both production bundles
build. Browser rendering, focus/keyboard behavior, responsive layouts, file picker,
token dialog/session persistence and visible cross-site polling/approval feedback
have not been visually verified for this integration. Live model behavior and
hosted deployment are also unverified. Existing visual tokens and layout classes
are preserved; no dependency, deployment, commit or push is part of this task.

## Implementation boundaries

- Each app's `src/lib/api.ts` configures the shared, browser-safe typed client in
  `packages/contracts/src/client.ts`; all successful payloads are Zod-validated.
- Workspace routes use `{ ok, data }`; suggest uses `{ ok, suggestion }`; context
  and shipments return their data directly. The client normalizes these into a
  discriminated `{ ok, data, error }` result and catches network/parse failures.
- `fixture-*` components are selected only by `NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_FIXTURES=1`.
  `packages/demo` is not consulted by API-backed components.
- Evidence bytes are served from the API; seeded JPEGs are labeled illustrations.
  The Customer site keeps the existing Lan scenario; CS lists all conversations.

# Design System: seaPilot

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "Continuity in blue"**

The shared interface uses cobalt actions, midnight brand framing, small cyan accents and cool light working surfaces. Customer support feels reassuring and spacious; the CS workspace is compact and evidence-led. Both use familiar task controls and precise status copy.

This is a code-led record of the current local frontend. Source files are `packages/ui/src/styles.css`, `packages/ui/src/index.tsx`, the official shadcn sources in `packages/ui/src/components/` and the components in both apps. Page strategy remains in `.impeccable/surfaces/`; this document records shared visual behavior.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Cobalt actions on light surfaces, with midnight and cyan brand framing.
- An original connected-path mark and pattern express continuity between contacts.
- Spacious customer conversation; compact agent workspace.
- Source labels, explicit approval controls and honest demo status.

## Colors

### Primary

Cobalt identifies primary actions and active navigation. A darker cobalt marks hover. Pale blue secondary buttons offer a quieter route into a draft. The focus color provides a visible keyboard outline.

### Brand framing

Midnight navy frames the Customer header and CS navigation rail. Signal cyan accents the original mark and connected-path motif; never use cyan as body text on white. The palette takes visual cues from the Sea × OpenAI Codex Hackathon reference, while the mark and pattern are original seaPilot assets. See `docs/BRANDING.md` and `docs/brand/seaPilot-brand-board.svg`; these are not partner logos or an endorsement.

### Neutral

White surfaces sit on a cool pale canvas. The `rail` token is a light hover/empty-state surface; the actual navigation rail uses `navy`. Dark blue ink carries content; muted blue-gray supports metadata. Light borders divide working panes without heavy framing.

### Semantic accents

System facts use green badges, customer claims use blue, and unverified claims use amber. Neutral badges carry identifiers and fixture labels. Error copy uses the error token. Always pair these colors with visible text.

**The Source Label Rule.** Preserve the visible source word; color alone never establishes a fact's provenance.

## Typography

The current UI body and controls use Arial with Helvetica and sans-serif fallbacks. Semibold labels separate actions and section headings from regular prose. Timestamps use tabular numerals.

Implemented hierarchy: the customer introduction is 36px, reducing to 29px on mobile; the workspace heading is 20px, reducing to 18px. Conversation bubbles in both sites use 16px with 1.7 line-height; agent density comes from pane structure and metadata, not smaller message text. Mobile composer text is 16px. These describe the build, not a new display-type standard. Compact metadata and badges currently descend to 9–11px; do not extend that density to new essential content without a legibility review.

## Layout

The customer site has an 80px header and a centered main container capped at 1120px including 32px side padding. Its chat and 286px order aside use a 24px gap. Below 768px, chat comes first, the aside follows in normal flow, and side padding becomes 16px. The order panel is not collapsible in the current build; earlier conversations use the shared shadcn Accordion. Mobile message height uses `clamp(220px,32dvh,320px)`.

The agent workspace fills `100dvh`. A 76px rail precedes a 248px inbox, flexible thread with a 320px minimum, and 370px case pane. At 1600px, the inbox and case pane grow to 290px and 420px. Below 1280px the case pane moves into a right-side sheet and the inbox is 240px. Below 768px the rail disappears and either inbox or selected thread occupies the width. Each long pane scrolls independently; composers remain outside message scroll regions.

Spacing centers on 8px, 16px and 24px with contextual 10px, 12px, 14px, 20px and 22px steps. Standard buttons are at least 40px tall, increasing to 44px on mobile. Compact buttons also maintain 40px desktop and 44px mobile minimum heights. Mobile filter tabs are at least 44px tall, and icon buttons are 44px wide.

## Elevation & Depth

Pane borders and tonal surfaces provide most depth. Cards are flat. The right-side sheet uses a structural shadow (`-8px 0 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 12%)`) above a dim overlay (`rgb(18 38 30 / 35%)`). Select popovers use the registry overlay shadow; ordinary cards and buttons suppress registry shadows. Composer focus adds a small tonal ring rather than elevating the whole form.

**The Flat Surface Rule.** Use borders and tonal differences for ordinary containers; reserve the structural shadow for overlays.

## Shapes

Controls use softly rounded corners, with a larger radius for the composer and prominent customer panels. Badges have compact corners; avatars are circular. Message bubbles have one square upper corner indicating the sender side. Evidence tiles crop their illustration region within a small bordered frame. Keep these shapes functional and consistent across both sites.

## Components

### Component foundation

Use the owned official shadcn New York components: Button, Badge, Card, Input, Textarea, Label, Select, Tabs, Accordion, Avatar, Sheet and Alert. Product wrappers supply sizing, colors and focus return. Applications use these controls rather than raw button/input/textarea/select/details elements; native document landmarks, forms, headings and text remain semantic HTML. Badge intentionally renders an inline span for use within source-labelled paragraphs. See `packages/ui/SHADCN-SOURCES.md` for registry provenance and adaptations.

### Buttons

Primary, outline, ghost and secondary variants share semibold labels, an 8px icon gap and the control radius. Outline and ghost hover use the rail surface. Secondary hover deepens its pale blue background. Buttons transition background and text color over 160ms with ease; disabled buttons reduce opacity to .48 and do not accept pointer interactions. Keyboard focus uses a 3px focus outline with 3px offset. Reduced-motion preferences remove transitions.

### Fields and composer

The composer groups a labelled textarea and actions inside a bordered rounded frame. Focus within changes the border and adds a two-pixel pale blue ring. Search uses a compact border and its own two-pixel focus outline. Hidden labels retain accessible field names. Mobile textarea sizing prevents undersized entry text.

### Badges and navigation

Source badges spell out System, Customer and Unverified. Case metadata carries System provenance; the team label is marked Unverified. Status badges similarly include text. Selected inbox rows gain a pale blue fill; active filter Tabs use cobalt text and a two-pixel underline. Radix Tabs provide keyboard selection and associated panels. The desktop identity rail uses icon controls with accessible names. Mobile uses an explicit back-to-inbox control and a case-details trigger.

### Panels, sheets and evidence

The customer order card has a light border and generous padding. The agent case pane uses divided sections, a tinted shipment-change block and a separate missing-fact area. Reply approval and escalation approval remain separate controls. The shadcn Sheet over Radix Dialog provides a title, description, close control and focus return. Evidence tiles use inline parcel artwork and the label Sample attachment; their detail view explains that no actual photo was supplied.
